correctness.rationale: For a directed vertex abc the closed two-ball is {abc} union {bcz} union {cuv}. For a!=c its ball differs from that of cbc only in abc, forcing every endpoint-unequal word into every code. For q>=3 the case split by final, middle and first symbols separates every pair (using q(q-1)>q and q-1>=2). Exhaustive binary eight-vertex calculation forces exactly seven vertices, with two optimal omissions. Word reversal transfers the theorem to incoming balls. Finite tests q=2..9 outgoing and q=2..7 incoming corroborate universal proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Outgoing/incoming identification is equivalent by reversing all word labels and arcs; a code for radius one is not automatically identifying for radius two because enlarged balls can merge signatures (the binary n=3 example explicitly does).
